title: 🤖 iOS/visionOS: Xcode exports include the other platform's camera placeholder xcframeworks
body:
> [!INFO] *AI disclosure*: This contribution was authored by an autonomous AI agent (Claude Code), on behalf of a user (@twcclegg), to report a packaging bug found while testing visionOS exports.

### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.8.dev7.official [c971f93e7]
- The cause is still present in godot-build-scripts `main` (4adf7c2, 2026-10-09).

### System information

macOS 27.0.1, Apple M1, Xcode 27.0 (27A266a), visionOS SDK 27.0. Device: Apple Vision Pro, visionOS 27.2 (24N5103f). It also reproduces with a project-only export from the Linux editor (Linux Mint 22.3, x86_64), since no Xcode step is involved.

### Issue description

Exporting a project for visionOS copies `libgodot_camera.ios.debug.xcframework` and `libgodot_camera.ios.release.xcframework` into the exported Xcode project. These are iOS placeholders, with `empty` files in their slices. This happens even though the camera module is not enabled (`modules/camera` is left at its default, `false`). The reverse also happens: iOS exports get the `libgodot_camera.visionos.*` placeholders.

**Cause: packaging.** `misc/dist/apple_embedded_xcode` holds placeholder xcframeworks for both platforms. That includes `libgodot_camera.ios.*` and `libgodot_camera.visionos.*`. When godot-build-scripts packages each platform's template zip, it only removes the *other* platform's `libgodot` placeholders, not its camera placeholders:

- [`build-release.sh` L400](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-build-scripts/blob/4adf7c2cdc53091130adcff5f9afa5358018de86/build-release.sh#L400) (visionOS): `rm -rf visionos_xcode/libgodot.ios.*`. This leaves `libgodot_camera.ios.*` in `visionos.zip`.
- [`build-release.sh` L383](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-build-scripts/blob/4adf7c2cdc53091130adcff5f9afa5358018de86/build-release.sh#L383) (iOS): `rm -rf ios_xcode/libgodot.visionos.*`. This leaves `libgodot_camera.visionos.*` in `ios.zip`.

Going by the script, the Mono and .NET iOS blocks ([L531](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-build-scripts/blob/4adf7c2cdc53091130adcff5f9afa5358018de86/build-release.sh#L531), [L686](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-build-scripts/blob/4adf7c2cdc53091130adcff5f9afa5358018de86/build-release.sh#L686)) don't remove *any* visionOS placeholders, so their `ios.zip` also carries `libgodot.visionos.*`. Confirmed in the official 4.8.dev7 Mono `ios.zip`, which has all four `libgodot*.visionos.*` placeholders, and an iOS export with it copies all four into the project.

**Why the exporter copies them:** `EditorExportPlatformAppleEmbedded::_export_project_helper` ([`editor_export_platform_apple_embedded.cpp` L2001 on master 232e6b1](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/232e6b14abf6e590b41d60f11704e42de22bff72/editor/export/editor_export_platform_apple_embedded.cpp#L2001)) only treats a `libgodot*` entry as a library, to be filtered or renamed, if its path contains the platform name:

```cpp
} else if (file.begins_with("libgodot") && file.contains(get_platform_name())) {
```

The stray entries never name the platform being exported (`libgodot_camera.ios.*` doesn't contain `visionos`, and `libgodot_camera.visionos.*` doesn't contain `ios`). So they skip the library filter, fall through to the generic copy, and are written into the project unchanged. The filter itself already matches libraries by exact, platform-qualified prefix, so it would skip them if it saw them.

**Contents of the official 4.8.dev7 templates** (from `unzip -l`):

| zip | `libgodot_camera.ios.*` | `libgodot_camera.visionos.*` |
|---|---|---|
| `visionos.zip` | placeholders only (`Info.plist` and `empty`, no `.a`) | real `libgodot_camera.a` in `xros-arm64` (debug 86712 bytes, release 83536 bytes) |
| `ios.zip` | real `libgodot_camera.a` in both slices | placeholders only (`Info.plist` and `empty`) |

In the visionOS export, the real `libgodot_camera.visionos.*` frameworks are correctly left out (camera is off). The `libgodot_camera.ios.*` placeholders are copied in, but nothing in `project.pbxproj` references them.

**Impact:** low. The exported project still builds and links (we built, linked and signed a visionOS device build with GDExtensions using Xcode 27.0). But every visionOS export ships two unused iOS placeholder xcframeworks, and by the same logic every iOS export ships two unused visionOS ones.

**Suggested fix (either, or both):**
- godot-build-scripts: also remove the other platform's camera placeholders, e.g. `rm -rf visionos_xcode/libgodot.ios.* visionos_xcode/libgodot_camera.ios.*` (and `libgodot_camera.visionos.*` for iOS).
- Exporter: send every `libgodot*` entry through the existing exact-prefix matching, by dropping the `file.contains(get_platform_name())` gate. That also covers custom templates and any future Apple embedded platform that shares this folder.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install the official 4.8.dev7 export templates.
2. In any project, add a visionOS export preset with `application/export_project_only=true`. Leave `modules/camera` off.
3. Export, e.g. `godot --headless --path . --export-debug "visionOS" out/app.xcodeproj`.
4. Look at the export folder: `libgodot_camera.ios.debug.xcframework` and `libgodot_camera.ios.release.xcframework` are there.
5. Likewise, an iOS export contains `libgodot_camera.visionos.{debug,release}.xcframework`.
6. Confirm they come from the template: `unzip -l visionos.zip | grep camera` lists both `libgodot_camera.ios.*` (placeholders) and `libgodot_camera.visionos.*` (real libraries). Likewise, `ios.zip` contains `libgodot_camera.visionos.*` placeholders.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Not needed: any project reproduces it, e.g. an empty project with one scene, since the stray files come from the export template, not the project.
